messages.author: f8d4b01284bd23d5
messages.subject: PMLR Output
parts:
Hi all,
I have several questions regrading the output I receive when using  the Penalized Multinomial Logistic Regression (PMLR) package:
I am working on a data-set that includes a dependent variable which has a multinomial logistic distribution (Israeli Supreme Court decisions regarding appeals which have three values: reject, partially accept and accept). I have several questions regrading the PMLR output I receive when running my models:
1. When running summary(mymodel) I receive a set of outcomes including three columns with OR at the column head. What does OR stand for? 
2. When running print(mymodel) I get the following:
$separation
, , 2

 (Intercept) Electoral.Comp ENP gamson.compa.all CIEP Composition framer.party.seats
          NA             NA  NA               NA   NA          NA                 NA
Does that mean that no separation exists in the model?
3. Also I get attr(,"class")
[1] "pmlr"
Does that (like in logistf) means that the model is indeed a penalized maximum likelihood regression object and should be estimated as such?
Thanks in advance,
Maoz

messages.author: 149440eddb848db9
messages.subject: Re: PMLR Output
parts:
Hi, Maoz

This topic of this mailing list RRO, the downstream distribution of R. Specifically, we will respond to any issues in the build process or functionality we add to R, e.g. the Intel MKL.

Your question is a statistics question about a specific package. Your best course of action would be to study the package documentation or any references about the model that the package implements.

Failing that, I suggest you post a question on CrossValidated (http://stats.stackexchange.com/) and tag the question as [R].

Good luck.

Andrie
